purpose: Evidence register for the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Each claim separates official commitments from implemented outcomes and preserves the next evidence needed.

status_legend.confirmed: Supported directly by an official or primary record.
status_legend.reported: Supported by credible reporting; relevant primary implementation records are still sought.
status_legend.not_yet_documented: The decisive public evidence has not yet been located in this dossier.
status_legend.not_established: Available evidence does not establish the claim.
status_legend.contradiction_open: Credible sources conflict; human review must retain both until resolved.

claims.claim: India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 12–13 September 2026.
claims.source: Government of India, Ministry of External Affairs
claims.limitation: Event hosting does not establish the effect of summit commitments.

claims.claim: BRICS leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration.
claims.source: New Delhi Declaration, republication of Prime Minister’s Office release
claims.limitation: The declaration proves consensus language; it does not prove delivery, financing or impact.

claims.claim: The declaration launched a common BRICS currency.
claims.source: New Delhi Declaration; The Indian Express analysis
claims.limitation: The reviewed material describes local-currency settlement and payment-system interoperability, not a launched shared currency.
claims.next_evidence_needed: A formally adopted common-currency instrument, governance structure, issuance mechanism and participating-country implementation record.

claims.claim: The declaration advances work on interoperable cross-border payments and local-currency financing.
claims.source: New Delhi Declaration; The Indian Express analysis
claims.limitation: It does not identify every operational corridor, access rule, fee, privacy control, remedy or live service outcome.

claims.claim: The summit’s payment work will help ordinary people and small businesses.
claims.limitation: A policy direction is not evidence of affordability, usability, consumer protection or inclusion.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Named live corridors, operators, fees, transaction limits, consumer recourse, language and disability accessibility, privacy rules and independent user evidence.

claims.claim: The declaration supports Global South-oriented AI cooperation and digital public infrastructure proposals.
claims.source: New Delhi Declaration; The Indian Express analysis
claims.limitation: The reviewed documents do not yet supply complete public rules on data sovereignty, energy, local language, accessibility, labour or independent oversight.

claims.claim: Nigeria is a BRICS partner country, not a full member.
claims.source: Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, Nigeria; AP
claims.limitation: Partner status does not establish a named benefit from the New Delhi summit.

claims.claim: Nigeria’s BRICS partnership has produced a named, publicly documented benefit from the New Delhi summit.
claims.limitation: Attendance and partnership status are not a public-benefit record.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Published agreements, project documents, financing terms, eligibility rules, implementation timeline and locally verifiable outcomes.

claims.claim: BRICS has become an effective peace mediator in West Asia.
claims.limitation: Calls for restraint and diplomacy are not a mediation mandate, named process or measured civilian-protection outcome.
claims.next_evidence_needed: A mandate, named mediators, consent of relevant parties, benchmarked actions and evidence of civilian protection.

claims.claim: Saudi Arabia’s present full-member status can be stated as settled across reliable sources.
claims.source: Indian official BRICS material; wire reporting of the New Delhi Declaration
claims.limitation: Indian official material describes an 11-country grouping including Saudi Arabia; several wire reports list 10 and omit it.
claims.next_evidence_needed: A current primary BRICS membership record that resolves the public discrepancy.
